question: Can Lumo's Select, Menu and ComboBox be rebuilt on Base UI without changing their public API, and what does that cost?

vendor_first.rule: CONTRIBUTING.md — never hand-type a component upstream already has.

fetched.note: There is no `menu` item in base-vega. The Base UI menu ships under three product names — dropdown-menu, menubar, context-menu — all 200, all importing `@base-ui/react/menu`. `dropdown-menu` (9439 chars) is the one whose composition Lumo's `menu.tsx` corresponds to and is what was used.

vendored_code_not_usable_verbatim: Every emit renders icons through `IconPlaceholder` from `@/app/(create)/components/icon-placeholder`, which is shadcn's own site component and is not in the registry payload.
Every emit is physical-utility-first: `pr-2 pl-2.5`, `pr-8 pl-2`, `right-2`, `ml-auto`, `text-left`. Lumo's lint bans all of them.

shadcn's submenu positions with `side="right"` — a physical side, on a library whose `Side` union carries `inline-start`/`inline-end`. Copied as-is it would open submenus on the wrong side in Persian and nothing would look wrong in review.

shadcn's dropdown-menu uses `MenuPrimitive.Separator`; `@base-ui/react/menu` 1.7.0 re-exports `Separator` from the shared `../separator/Separator.js` rather than owning one, so the part resolves but not from where the emit implies.
vendor_first.what_it_was_worth: The composition. Base UI's Select is Root→Trigger→Value/Icon→Portal→Positioner→Popup→List→Item→ItemText→ItemIndicator; guessing that from the type declarations alone would have taken longer than reading it. The styling was not worth anything — it was rewritten to Lumo's existing variant strings.

test_bar.actual: THOSE FILES DO NOT EXIST. `select.test.tsx`, `menu.test.tsx` and `combobox.test.tsx` are absent from packages/ui/src. The conformance bar for all three lives in `overlays.test.tsx`, whose header names dialog.tsx, popover.tsx, menu.tsx, select.tsx, combobox.tsx and breadcrumbs.tsx as the batch it pins. `menubar.test.tsx` and `context-menu.test.tsx` import from menu.tsx as well; `coverage.test.ts` enumerates the filesystem and grades all three mechanically.

method.contamination_warning: The working tree is shared. While this rebuild was in progress a sibling agent rebuilt popover.tsx, dialog.tsx, tabs.tsx, tooltip.tsx, slider.tsx and number-field.tsx on Base UI in the same checkout. Results below are attributed per component; one overlays.test.tsx failure belongs to dialog.tsx and is marked as not attributable to this rebuild. `tsc --noEmit` over the package reports errors in tooltip.tsx (6), tabs.tsx (3), slider.tsx (1) and number-field.tsx (1) that are not from these three files — select.tsx, menu.tsx and combobox.tsx typecheck clean.

before_change.command: pnpm --filter @lumo-ui/ui exec vitest run src/overlays.test.tsx src/menubar.test.tsx src/context-menu.test.tsx src/coverage.test.ts
before_change.note: Taken against the React Aria implementations before any edit. This is the green the rebuild is measured against.

api_preservation.claim: The public API did not change.

evidence.check: apps/website typechecks against the rebuilt components
evidence.what_it_covers: Every real consumer in the repo — apps/website/src/examples/{select,menu,menubar}.tsx, apps/website/src/lib/demos.tsx (ComboBox), apps/website/src/components/site-shell.tsx (the locale-switcher Menu of `href` items) — compiles unchanged against the Base UI implementations. The props those call sites pass (placeholder, className, aria-label, defaultSelectedKey, isDisabled, textValue, id, label, showSuggestionsLabel, suggestionsLabel, href, hrefLang, title, onAction) all survived.

evidence.result: zero diagnostics in select.tsx, menu.tsx and combobox.tsx
evidence.note: Diagnostics elsewhere in the package belong to sibling agents' in-flight files; see method.contamination_warning.

evidence.check: coverage.test.ts — the mechanical rules, applied to every .tsx in the package
evidence.what_it_covers: All three files are still exported from the barrel, still declare "use client", still hardcode no English default for an announced string, and still keep no `cva` that a server module reaches for.

failures.test: a plain modal dialog is clean; isDismissable on the OVERLAY adds one 'Dismiss'
failures.attributable_to: dialog.tsx (sibling agent's rebuild), NOT this one

failures.test: every open popover carries exactly two unreachable 'Dismiss' labels
failures.reading: The rebuild is BETTER than the assertion. React Aria bracketed every open popover with two visually-hidden DismissButtons labelled from `@react-aria/overlays`, unreachable by prop, and popover.tsx documented them as an accepted leak. Base UI's menu emits no dismiss button at all: an open Lumo menu now contributes zero announced English. The test is red because it pins React Aria's leak count as a number, not because anything got worse.

failures.test: MenuItem keeps typeahead text and marks submenus with an aria-hidden mirrored glyph
failures.reading: Base UI states the same fact with `aria-haspopup="menu"`; it has no `data-has-submenu`. Re-emitting React Aria's attribute name by hand was rejected — see capability gap `menu.has-submenu-attribute`.

failures.error: Base UI: MenuRootContext is missing. Menu parts must be placed within <Menu.Root>.
failures.reading: See capability gap `menu.virtual-trigger-anchoring`. This is the single largest breakage in the rebuild and it is in a DEPENDENT, not in menu.tsx itself.

attributable.test: Select renders the Persian placeholder, never RAC's 'Select an item'

notes: Base UI's trigger is `role="combobox" aria-haspopup="listbox"`; React Aria's was a plain button with the same haspopup. Both are valid select-only-combobox patterns; the announced role changes from "button" to "combobox".

Base UI renders a visually-hidden `<input>` into the FIRST BYTE even with no `name` prop: `<input id="…-hidden-input" style="clip-path:inset(50%);…" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true" value=""/>`. React Aria emitted nothing for an unnamed Select.

attributable.test: closed overlays contribute nothing at all to the first byte
every open popover carries exactly two unreachable 'Dismiss' labels
MenuItem keeps typeahead text and marks submenus with an aria-hidden mirrored glyph

verified_working.trigger_bridge: `<Menu.Trigger render={<Button/>}>` DRIVES a React Aria Button. Measured by firing a real click: aria-expanded went false→true, one `[role=menu]` and one `[role=menuitem]` appeared. Base UI's props land on the RAC Button intact: aria-haspopup=menu, aria-expanded, aria-controls, id, data-popup-open, data-pressed. This was the biggest assumed risk in the port and it is not a risk.
verified_working.onAction: Synthesised through a Lumo context. `<Menu onAction>` + `<MenuItem id="copy">` fired with `["copy"]`.
verified_working.sections: `<MenuSection title>` renders `Menu.Group` + `Menu.GroupLabel`; the group's `aria-labelledby` resolves to the title text (measured: "ویرایش").
verified_working.links: `<MenuItem href hrefLang>` routes to `Menu.LinkItem`, emitting `<a role="menuitem" href="/fa-IR/x" hreflang="fa-IR">` — the shape apps/website/src/components/site-shell.tsx's locale switcher needs.

attributable.test: ComboBox closes both of RAC's English aria-labels

defect_found_and_fixed_during_the_port.what: The first composition used `<Combobox.Label>`, the part whose name says it is the label. It renders a `<div>`, and it labels the TRIGGER, not the input.
defect_found_and_fixed_during_the_port.base_ui_says_so_itself: ComboboxLabel.mjs logs, in dev: '<Combobox.Label> labels <Combobox.Trigger> only. When <Combobox.Input> is the form control, use a native <label> or <Field.Label> instead.'
defect_found_and_fixed_during_the_port.fix: Pass a `useId()` to `Combobox.Root` (which becomes the input's id) and render a native `<label htmlFor>`. SSR-stable, so the pairing is in the first byte.
defect_found_and_fixed_during_the_port.why_it_matters: React Aria wired exactly this composition through LabelContext with nothing asked of the caller. Under Base UI the correct-looking part produced an unnamed text field, and nothing on screen or in a screenshot would have shown it.

capability_gaps.lumo_api_promise: context-menu.tsx composes `MenuPopover` + `Menu` under a React Aria `MenuTrigger` whose `PopoverContext.triggerRef` is overridden to a portaled 1-point anchor at the pointer.
capability_gaps.base_ui_position: Every `Menu.Portal`/`Positioner`/`Popup` must be inside a `Menu.Root`; there is no context whose anchor a foreign parent can substitute. Base UI's answer is a separate product, `@base-ui/react/context-menu`, with its own `ContextMenu.Root` and `ContextMenu.Trigger`.
capability_gaps.evidence: Base UI: MenuRootContext is missing. Menu parts must be placed within <Menu.Root>. — thrown from @base-ui/react/menu/portal/MenuPortal.mjs:23, on all 4 context-menu.test.tsx tests, in both the renderToStaticMarkup and the jsdom arms.
capability_gaps.not_faked: menu.tsx was NOT given an escape hatch to satisfy context-menu.tsx. Porting context-menu.tsx means adopting `@base-ui/react/context-menu`, which is a different component with a different trigger contract — a separate decision, not a patch to this one.
capability_gaps.cost_if_adopted: context-menu.tsx (7178 bytes) is rewritten, not adapted. Its `createPortal` anchor, its `PopoverContext.Consumer/Provider` swap and its Shift+F10 handler all disappear, and Base UI supplies the behaviour instead — which is a smaller file, but a full rewrite and a fresh set of measurements.

capability_gaps.severity: visible wrong text on a shipped example
capability_gaps.lumo_api_promise: `<Select defaultSelectedKey="thr">` shows the matching item's text in the collapsed control. apps/website/src/examples/select.tsx's `DisabledExample` depends on it.
capability_gaps.base_ui_position: `<Select.Value>` resolves a label only from the Root's `items` prop (`resolveSelectedLabel` in internals/resolveValueLabel.mjs consults `store.items` and never the mounted items). The items live inside a portal that renders null while closed, so there is nothing to read.
capability_gaps.evidence: renderToStaticMarkup of `
capability_gaps.not_faked: The obvious workaround is to walk `children` for a matching `id` and lift its text. That is a collection builder inside a wrapper — the exact work renting a headless library is supposed to buy — so it was left honest and recorded here.
capability_gaps.workaround_available_to_a_caller: Pass Base UI's own `items` shape to the Root. That is a different public API from React Aria's collection and would be an API change, so it was not done.

capability_gaps.severity: would fail @lumo-ui/gate's `named-controls` rule on a shipped page
capability_gaps.lumo_api_promise: `<Select placeholder=…><Label>شهر</Label><SelectTrigger/>…` — the composition every example in apps/website/src/examples/select.tsx uses.
capability_gaps.base_ui_position: Lumo's shared `<Label>` (form.tsx) is React Aria's `Label`, which names a control by picking up `LabelContext` from an RAC ancestor. Base UI publishes no such context, and its own `Select.Label` renders a `<div>` that names the trigger through an internal store.
capability_gaps.evidence: Rendered `<Select><Label>شهر</Label><SelectTrigger/>…`: the label emitted `<label class="w-fit text-sm font-medium text-fg select-none">شهر</label>` with NO `for`; the trigger carried no `aria-label` and no `aria-labelledby`; computed accessible name = null.
capability_gaps.not_faked: `Select` cannot intercept a `<Label>` the caller passes as a child without inspecting element types, and form.tsx is outside this brief.
capability_gaps.cost_if_adopted: Either every Lumo control rebuilt on Base UI takes an explicit `aria-label`, or form.tsx's `Label` learns to emit `htmlFor` and every Base UI-based component publishes its control id. This is the class of defect the repo's own ledger is made of: it renders, it type-checks, it looks right, and the control is nameless.

capability_gaps.severity: one red assertion, no behavioural loss
capability_gaps.lumo_api_promise: Not a prop — a DOM state contract overlays.test.tsx pins: `data-has-submenu` on a submenu's trigger item.
capability_gaps.base_ui_position: `Menu.SubmenuTrigger` publishes `data-popup-open`, `data-highlighted`, `data-disabled`. The 'has a submenu' fact is stated as `aria-haspopup="menu"`, which it does set (measured).
capability_gaps.not_faked: The attribute is trivially forgeable — this component knows at composition time that it is a submenu trigger — and was deliberately not forged. Writing React Aria's attribute name onto a Base UI element makes the test green while making the DOM lie about which library it came from, and every later measurement reads that DOM.

capability_gaps.lumo_api_promise: `<MenuTrigger trigger="longPress">`, which menu.tsx's header documented (together with the English `aria-describedby` React Aria attached when you used it).
capability_gaps.base_ui_position: `Menu.Root` has no long-press trigger. Nearest neighbours are `openOnHover`, `delay`, `closeDelay` on `Menu.Trigger`.
capability_gaps.not_faked: The prop is gone from the type rather than accepted and ignored. Silver lining: the unreachable English string it dragged in is gone with it.

capability_gaps.lumo_api_promise: React Aria's `items` + render-function children on `Menu` and `MenuSection`.
capability_gaps.base_ui_position: `Menu` has no collection at all — no `items`, no `Collection`, no render-function children. (Base UI's `Combobox` and `Select` do have `items`; `Menu` does not.)
capability_gaps.not_faked: `MenuSectionProps.items` is typed `Iterable<T> & never`, so passing one is a compile error rather than a value that renders nothing.

capability_gaps.base_ui_position: `Select.List` takes none of them. There is no empty state, no dependency array and no multi-selection through this path (`Select.Root` has a `multiple` prop, which is a different API from React Aria's `selectionMode`).
capability_gaps.not_faked: Removed from the type rather than accepted and dropped.

capability_gaps.severity: silent behaviour loss for one of two documented usages
capability_gaps.lumo_api_promise: Both forms filter as you type: static `<ComboBoxItem>` children, and `items` + a render function.
capability_gaps.base_ui_position: Filtering happens on the ROOT, over the `items` array, via `filter`/`itemToStringLabel`. With static children and no `items`, `Combobox.List` receives plain ReactNode children and nothing filters them. React Aria's collection builder filtered either form.
capability_gaps.not_faked: The `items` + render-function form is wired through and does filter. The static-children form renders and navigates but does not narrow, and that is stated here rather than papered over — note that this is the form apps/website/src/lib/demos.tsx uses.

capability_gaps.base_ui_position: `Select.Item` and `Menu.Item` both take `label` for keyboard text matching. `Combobox.Item` takes none — matching is a root-level concern.
capability_gaps.not_faked: It is not forwarded to `aria-label`, which would have made the test-visible symptom disappear while renaming every option after its own visible text.

capability_gaps.what: `SelectProps<T>`, `SelectValueProps<T>`, `SelectItemProps<T>`, `MenuItemProps<T>`, `MenuSectionProps<T>` and `ComboBoxItemProps<T>` had `T` only because they extended a React Aria props type carrying a collection generic. With no collection there is nothing left for `T` to type, and `noUnusedParameters` makes an unused type parameter a compile error.
capability_gaps.resolution: Each keeps one documented field typed `T & never` (or `Iterable<T> & never`), so the type PARAMETER survives — a `SelectProps<City>` annotation a consumer already wrote still compiles — while passing a value is a compile error rather than a prop that is accepted and silently dropped.
capability_gaps.not_faked: The alternative, typing them `T | undefined` and ignoring them at runtime, is the accepted-and-dropped shape this project treats as a defect.

capability_gaps.component: all three (and every other Base UI rebuild in this experiment)
capability_gaps.severity: silent LTR on every Persian page
capability_gaps.what: Base UI resolves direction from `DirectionProvider`, whose `direction` defaults to `'ltr'` (DirectionProvider.mjs: `const { direction = 'ltr' } = props`). Lumo's `LumoProvider` (packages/ui/src/provider.tsx) mounts only React Aria's `I18nProvider`, so nothing sets Base UI's direction.
capability_gaps.consequence: Logical sides (`inline-start`/`inline-end`) resolve as if the document were LTR: a submenu opens on the wrong side in Persian, and arrow-key direction follows suit. The markup is individually valid and the failure is inline geometry — the same profile provider.tsx's own header describes for the React Aria case.
capability_gaps.not_faked: provider.tsx was NOT edited; it is outside this brief and provider.test.tsx pins its current behaviour. Recorded so that whoever decides the experiment knows a Base UI adoption is a provider change too, not only a component change.

english_strings.question: Which English does Base UI emit that no prop reaches?
english_strings.method: grep over the shipped dist of @base-ui/react/{select,menu,combobox} for `aria-label`/`aria-roledescription`/`title` literals and for sentence-shaped string literals.

found.why: `ComboboxInternalDismissButton` is marked `@internal` and is constructed by ComboboxPopup.mjs and ComboboxInput.mjs with no props at all (`<ComboboxInternalDismissButton ref={…} />`), so there is no argument to override.
found.when_rendered: Only while the popup is open AND focus management is modal; it is a visually-hidden `<span>`. Not in the served bytes — the SSR sweep of the closed component found zero Latin announced strings.
found.measured_in_this_rebuild: The open-state sweep of the composition Lumo ships did NOT surface it (open ComboBox spoken attributes = ["button[aria-label]=نمایش پیشنهادها"]). It is recorded because the literal exists and a different modal configuration would emit it.

not_found: No `aria-roledescription` anywhere in the three components.
No string bundle, no locale files, no `IntlTranslations`-style dictionary of any kind — the surface a Persian translation would have to cover is one word long.

react_aria_comparison.select: `selectPlaceholder: "Select an item"` — VISIBLE English in the first byte when `placeholder` is unset. Reachable, and that is why Lumo's `placeholder` is required.
react_aria_comparison.combobox: `buttonLabel: "Show suggestions"` and `listboxLabel: "Suggestions"` — reachable, and that is why Lumo's two label props are required.
react_aria_comparison.popover_menu_select_combobox: Two unreachable `aria-label="Dismiss"` per open popover, from RAC's bracketing DismissButtons.
react_aria_comparison.net: React Aria emitted 3 reachable strings and 2 unreachable ones per open overlay across these three components. Base UI emits 0 reachable and 1 unreachable, and the unreachable one did not appear in the composition Lumo ships.

english_strings.the_inversion_that_matters: Every required-string prop in these three components survived the port, and every one of them changed its justification. React Aria shipped the WRONG LANGUAGE; Base UI ships NOTHING. An unset `placeholder` used to render «Select an item» into a Persian form — ugly, and catchable by a gate that grades Latin text. Under Base UI it renders an EMPTY control, and an icon-only `Combobox.Trigger` with no `aria-label` is a nameless button. Neither leaves a Latin word behind, so `no-latin-aria` cannot see either one. The props are required for a stronger reason after the port than before it.

state_attributes.why: button.tsx rule 5 says state comes from React Aria's `data-*` attributes styled with Tailwind `data-` variants. That rule is engine-coupled: every variant string naming a state had to be rewritten, and a missed one is a class that styles nothing and reviews as if it did.

data-hovered.base_ui: NONE — Base UI emits no hover attribute on any part of these three

--trigger-width.note: A CSS custom property, not a class. Left alone it silently shrink-wraps the panel; nothing would have failed.

state_attributes.focus_ring_survives: packages/theme/src/theme.css keys the single focus ring off `:where([data-lumo]):focus-visible` — a native pseudo-class, not an engine attribute — so `data-lumo` on Base UI elements works unchanged.

popoverVariants.reason: All three components render the same floating panel; four divergent copies is how a design system stops being one.
popoverVariants.measured_problem: As of this writing the shared cva still carries React Aria's transition selectors — `data-entering:`, `data-exiting:`, `data-[placement=bottom]:`, `data-[placement=top]:`. Under Base UI the equivalents are `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style` and `data-side`, so those four selectors are INERT in every Base UI component that composes this cva, including these three. Nothing fails; the panels simply appear without their enter/exit transition.
popoverVariants.not_fixed_here: popover.tsx is a sibling agent's file in the same working tree and was being rewritten concurrently. Flagged rather than edited.

placementToSideAlign.reason: One translation of React Aria's single-string placement vocabulary into Base UI's two-axis `side`+`align`, shared by every overlay. `menu.tsx` had its own `Record<LumoPlacement, …>` for about ten minutes and it was deleted in favour of the shared one.

LumoPlacement.reason: `MenuPopover`'s `placement` prop keeps its exact public type — `Exclude<AriaPlacement, …left… | …right…>` — with no React Aria runtime import. The type is erased at build.

structural_differences.what: React Aria's `Select`, `ComboBox` and `Menu` roots render a real element that `className` and `data-lumo` attach to. Base UI's `Select.Root`, `Combobox.Root` and `Menu.Root` render nothing at all.
structural_differences.consequence: Each rebuilt component adds a wrapper `<div>` inside the Root to keep `className` and `data-lumo` meaningful. `Menu` additionally carries `role="none"`, because Base UI puts `role="menu"` on `Menu.Popup` one level up and an unroled generic between a menu and its menuitems is not conforming.

structural_differences.what: React Aria's `MenuTrigger` renders no DOM and wires whatever control it is given through `ButtonContext`. Base UI's `Menu.Trigger` IS the control and adopts a foreign element only through its `render` prop.
structural_differences.consequence: `MenuTrigger` splits its children positionally and lifts child[0] into `render`. The public API is unchanged.
structural_differences.measured: The bridge works with Lumo's React Aria `<Button>`: a real click opened the menu, and Base UI's aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-controls/id/data-popup-open/data-pressed all landed on the RAC button.

structural_differences.what: React Aria's `SubmenuTrigger` took `[item, popover]` positionally. Base UI splits state (`Menu.SubmenuRoot`) from element (`Menu.SubmenuTrigger`).
structural_differences.consequence: `SubmenuTrigger` supplies the root and sets a Lumo context flag; `MenuItem` reads the flag and renders itself as `Menu.SubmenuTrigger` instead of `Menu.Item`. The caller's composition is unchanged.

structural_differences.what: React Aria published `'bottom start'` for a root menu and `'end top'` for a submenu through `PopoverContext`, so a `MenuPopover` that set nothing got both right. Base UI's `Menu.Positioner` defaults to `side="bottom" align="center"` at every level.
structural_differences.consequence: `MenuPopover` reads the nesting flag and reproduces React Aria's two defaults. A Base UI port that skipped this would open every submenu BELOW its parent item, in both directions, and look merely odd rather than broken.

structural_differences.what: React Aria treated `<MenuItem id>` as the collection key and generated its own DOM id. Base UI's `Menu.Item` `id` IS the DOM id.
structural_differences.consequence: `id` is deliberately not forwarded. Forwarded, it put the caller's key into the document (measured: `id=b`), and two menus offering the same action would emit duplicate ids with `aria-activedescendant` resolving to whichever came first.

observations.confidence: low — recorded as raw bytes, not as a claim
observations.what: `renderToStaticMarkup` of the ComboBox emits `<input … autoComplete="off" spellCheck="false" autoCorrect="off" autoCapitalize="none" …>` — camelCase attribute names in the served HTML. The same component in jsdom shows the normalised `autocomplete`/`spellcheck`/`autocorrect`/`autocapitalize`.
observations.impact: None known: HTML attribute names are case-insensitive, so both parse identically. Recorded because it is a difference in the served bytes and this project measures the served bytes.
